In case Buyer has selected Purchase preference to Micro and Small Enterprises clause in the bid, the same will get precedence over this clause. 8. Service & Support AVAILABILITY OF OFFICE OF SERVICE PROVIDER: An office of the Service Provider must be located in the state of Consignee. DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE TO BE SUBMITTED. 9. Service & Support Dedicated /toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support : BIDDER/OEM must have Dedicated/toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support. 10. Service & Support Escalation Matrix For Service Support : Bidder/OEM must provide Escalation Matrix of Telephone Numbers for Service Support. 11. Purchase Preference (State) Bid reserved for MSE from the State of Bid Inviting Authority: Procurement under this bid is reserved for purchase from Micro and Small Enterprises from the State of Bid Inviting Authority having valid Udyam Registration and whose credentials are validated online through Udyam Registration portal. Any other document in support of contract execution like Third Party Inspection release note, etc. 13. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses [1] Scope and price. Supply, install, configure, test and commission the complete IP-based CCTV system at KSMDB College, Sasthamcotta, and train designated staff as per the published BoQ. All equipment and accessories shall be new, genuine, unused, defect-free and mutually compatible. The bid price shall includ e freight, handling, installation, accessories, training and applicable taxes. [2] Unused installation materials. BoQ quantities for Cat6 cable, PVC conduit, optical fibre cable and si milar measurable materials are estimates. Where less is required, the seller and Inspection Committee sha ll jointly measure and record the installed quantities. The seller shall remove any unused balance brought to site at its own cost. Subject to the GeM contract, deduct the quantity difference at the contracted BoQ u nit rate and adjust applicable taxes. [3] Inspection and acceptance. Final acceptance requires satisfactory installation, testing, commissioni ng and training, verification of contractual compliance, and a favourable report from the College’s Inspecti on Committee. The Committee shall verify specifications, quantities, quality, compatibility and performanc e. [4] Rejected goods. The supplier shall remove defective, damaged, substandard or non-conforming good s at its own risk and cost within the period specified by the Buyer and replace them at no additional cost. [5] Transit and delivery. The supplier is responsible for safe delivery to the designated locations and sha ll make good any damage, theft, shortage or loss before delivery and acceptance at no additional cost. [6] Bank charges and payment. The supplier shall bear its bank charges and related expenses. Paymen t shall follow the applicable GeM General Terms and Conditions and contract terms. [7] Pre-bid meeting and site visit. Attendance is encouraged and shall be at the bidder’s expense. Non- attendance alone shall not disqualify a bidder. Attendees shall upload their attendance certificate with the technical bid. The Buyer shall publish the schedule, clarifications and changes on GeM, with schedule chan ges notified in advance by corrigendum. [8] Technical bid documents. Upload evidence of relevant CCTV or similar IP surveillance/networking ex perience and satisfactory past performance, plus a CA-certified turnover statement or relevant audited fin ancial statements, as prescribed in the bid and subject to applicable exemptions. Upload valid OEM authori sation covering supply and warranty support, or proof of OEM status. The bidder shall have a GeM seller ra ting of at least 4.0 out of 5.0 on the date of bid submission and upload verifiable proof. [09] Compatibility and commissioning. Cameras, NVRs, PoE switches, storage and networking accesso ries shall work together and meet the BoQ’s ONVIF requirements. Complete cable laying and termination, mounting, network and recording setup, and connectivity testing at the designated locations. Demonstrate the operation of all equipment, including power backup, before acceptance. [10] Warranty and Kerala service centres. Provide the applicable OEM and bid-specified warranty, incl uding repair, replacement, on-site assistance and escalation contacts. Each offered UPS, CCTV camera a nd NVR shall have support from an OEM-operated or OEM-authorised service centre in Kerala. Sub mit the centre’s name, full address, contact details and OEM proof with the technical bid. The supplier rem

ains responsible for warranty and support. [11] Training and handover. Train nominated staff in live monitoring, NVR operation, playback, footage retrieval and export, storage management, routine maintenance and basic troubleshooting. Hand over ma nuals, warranty documents, equipment details, installation layouts, configuration records and administrato r credentials securely. [12] Data security and confidentiality. Configure access controls and change default passwords during commissioning. Enable remote access only with the College’s written approval. Access, copying, retention or disclosure of footage requires specific College authorisation for installation, testing or maintenance. CCT V data shall remain under the College’s control. [13] Installation quality and safety. Use safe, professional installation practices and agree cable routes and equipment locations with the College. Protect existing property and infrastructure. The supplier shall r ectify damage caused by negligent installation at its own cost. [14] GeM conditions and evaluation. Applicable GeM terms and contract provisions shall govern in cas e of conflict. The Buyer may verify documents and seek technical clarifications under GeM procedures. Tec hnical qualification shall follow the eligibility criteria and specifications published before bid closing. . 14. Buyer Added Bid Specific SLA Text Clause(s) Buyer-Specific Service Level Agreement Supply, Installation, Testing, Training and Commissioning of an IP-Based CCTV Surveillance Sy stem Buyer and site Kumbalathu Sankupillai Memorial Devaswom Board College, Sasthamcotta, Kollam, Kerala - 690521 [1] Application and contract period This SLA applies to the successful service provider from the GeM contract start date through completion a nd final acceptance, and to support during the applicable warranty periods. Read it with the published bid, Scope of Work, Item Specification Document, Buyer-Added Additional Terms and Conditions (ATC) and appl icable GeM contract terms. [2] Delivery and installation Complete supply, installation, testing, training and commissioning within the period specified in the GeM c ontract. Coordinate camera locations, cable routes, work schedules and site access with the Buyer's desig nated representative. The Buyer shall nominate a point of contact, provide agreed site access and designa te staff for training. The service provider shall supply all labour, tools and materials within scope and rectif y damage caused by negligent installation at its own cost. [3] Commissioning, training and acceptance Demonstrate all 28 cameras and both NVRs, camera-to-NVR connectivity, live viewing, recording, playback , authorised footage export and backup. Verify Cat6 and optical fibre links, storage, access controls and th e minimum three-hour UPS backup specified in the contract. Record test results, rectify deficiencies and re peat the affected tests at no additional cost. Train the Buyer's nominated staff and hand over equipment and serial-number records, as-installed layout s, configuration records, test results, manuals, warranty certificates and escalation contacts. Transfer adm inistrator credentials securely. Final acceptance requires successful completion of these deliverables and a satisfactory report from the Buyer's Inspection Committee.

[4] Comprehensive warranty and local support Provide a minimum three-year comprehensive warranty from final acceptance for the IP cameras, NVRs, 2 TB surveillance hard disks, 5 TB external hard disk, PoE switches and online UPS including batteries. Apply the warranty stated in the contract to the remaining items. For covered faults, provide on-site diagnosis, tr avel, labour, parts, repair or replacement, and retesting at no additional cost. Each offered UPS, CCTV camera and NVR shall have an OEM-operated or OEM-authorised service centre in Kerala. The service provider shall coordinate support through the relevant centre and remains responsible for meeting this SLA. [5] Incident response and restoration The Buyer shall report faults through the designated phone or email. The service provider shall issue a co mplaint reference and record the reporting time, affected equipment and priority. Measure each deadline f rom the time the Buyer reports the fault through the designated channel. Critical faults. System-wide outage, loss of recording on any NVR, multiple camera outages from a share d fault, or failure of UPS backup. Acknowledge within 4 calendar hours. Attend on-site, where applicable, within 24 calendar hours. Restore service within 48 calendar hours. Standard faults. Single camera fault or other isolated issue that does not meet the critical criteria. Acknowledge within 1 working day. Attend on-site, where applicable, within 2 working days. Restore service within 5 working days. On-site attendance applies where remote resolution is unavailable or the Buyer requires a site visit. Calend ar hours run continuously. Working days are days on which the College administrative office is open. The s ervice clock may be paused for site access or other Buyer-side dependencies only for the period confirmed in writing by the Buyer. Restoration means return of the affected function to service. If permanent repair requires more time, the s ervice provider shall arrange a compatible temporary replacement or other Buyer-approved workaround w ithin the restoration deadline and provide a target date for permanent repair. The incident remains open u ntil the Buyer verifies the permanent fix. [6] Escalation and service records Provide a primary service contact and an escalation contact at handover. Notify the Buyer promptly if a de adline is at risk. Record the fault, diagnosis, attendance, action taken, parts replaced, restoration time and closure confirmation in a service report. Share the report with the Buyer after each incident. [7] Data security and confidentiality Change default passwords during commissioning and apply role-based access controls. Enable remote acc ess only with the Buyer's written approval. Access, copying, transfer or retention of footage by service per sonnel requires the Buyer's specific authorisation. All footage and associated data shall remain under the Buyer's control. [8] Payment and remedies Payment, acceptance and any remedies for delay or service shortfall shall follow the applicable GeM contr act provisions. The Buyer shall document missed deadlines and communicate required corrective action to the service provider. 16.
